newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra says tax deal lifts gas competition.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra says tax deal lifts gas competition.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday a deal with the state of Victoria and gas producers The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Exxon Corp over a petroleum tax would boost competition in the gas market.

Treasurer Peter Costello said the Petroleum Resource Rent (PRRT) tax agreement with the Bass Strait producers contained very significant pro-competitive reforms to contractual arrangements between the companies and major customer GASCOR.
"These changes will effectively remove GASCOR's exclusive contractual franchise and will allow other gas suppliers to enter the market on a competitive basis," Costello said.

Subsequent reforms to Victorian gas regulation, to be reviewed later this year, would also complement the reforms, he said in a statement. "The commitment of Victoria to the COAG (Council of Australian Governments) reforms to establish a competitive national gas market has been conditional on a satisfactory resolution of the PRRT dispute," he said.
"Today's agreement removes that condition and renews Victoria's commitment to the COAG reforms," Costello said.
As a result, the agreement also removed barriers to prospective interstate trade in gas.
-- removal of restrictions which prevented BHP or Exxon subsidiary Esso Resources Australia from selling gas, directly or indirectly, to consumers in Victoria;
-- relaxation of vertical ties between the producers and GASCOR;
-- removal of restrictions on BHP or Esso which prevented them from building pipelines in certain areas of Victoria;
-- removal of any restrictions on the right of GASCOR, Esso and BHP to market gas freely interstate;
-- removal of restrictions on customers of GASCOR from on-selling gas.
